## Dark theme hardening + first-start polish

Major iteration on the dark-mode experience and first-start UX. Several
startup dialogs that JDownloader normally shows to a user (tray
"isn't supported" error, FLATLAF Design-Update prompt, Extensions install
prompt) are now handled automatically by an in-process JVM agent — the
container starts to a usable UI without any clicks.

## Highlights

- **JVM dark-theme agent** (`/opt/JDownloader/jd-dark-agent.jar`) loaded via
  `-javaagent`. Two daemon threads:
  - **Colour thread** pushes Breeze Dark to UIManager and re-applies on every
    new window — so chrome, menus, popups all render dark from the moment JD
    starts, with no flicker.
  - **Dialog thread** polls `Window.getWindows()` and handles JD's startup
    dialogs automatically:
    - "Error" / "Fehler" containing *"Tray isn't supported"* → dispose silently
    - "Design-Update" → click OK so FLATLAF_DARK is registered (no re-prompt)
    - "Erweiterungen verwalten" / "Manage Extensions" → click *Jetzt installieren*
- **FlatLaf JAR patched** with explicit per-component Breeze Dark overrides
  (`Table.background`, `List.background`, `Panel.background`, `Viewport.background`,
  `TableHeader.background`, …) — over 60 component keys baked into
  `FlatDarkLaf.properties` so the LAF actually delivers the colours JD's stock
  renderer asks for.
- **Banner consolidation** — single source at `.github/assets/banner-raw.txt`,
  encoded with `tr -d '\r'` (byte-safe, was previously corrupted by `sed`
  running under POSIX locale).
- **LSIO base-image banner suppressed** — the `linuxserver.io` ASCII block
  and donate-URL printed by `init-adduser` no longer double up over our own
  banner. GID/UID setup logic is untouched.

## Force-Update reset fix

Containers installed via `wget` to a filename without the `my-` prefix
(e.g. `jdownloader.xml`) end up with a duplicate of Unraid's own
`my-JDownloader.xml`. dockerMan then can't reliably tell which file is the
authoritative one, and Force Update silently resets settings to template
defaults (network → none, ports → defaults).

The README install command now writes to `my-JDownloader.xml` directly, and
existing users with the lowercase variant can remove it once to fix the
behaviour:

```bash
rm /boot/config/plugins/dockerMan/templates-user/jdownloader.xml
```

The template XML itself also got back the `<Network>bridge</Network>` and
`<TemplateURL>` tags that were briefly removed — Unraid relies on them to
preserve user customizations across Force Update.

## Cleanups

- Removed the abandoned Xvfb-based pre-install (`scripts/pre-install-jd.sh`)
  — CI could only capture a partial snapshot that broke user installs more
  than it helped. The JVM agent supersedes it.
- `cont-init.d` no longer carries an inline tray-disable heredoc; calls
  `disable-tray.py` instead.
- README: `JD_THEME` description aligned with the template's actual values
  (`Dark` / `Light`), filesystem tree fixed.
- `.gitignore` now ignores `__pycache__/`.

## Known limitation (unchanged)

JD's custom download list / link grabber renderer (`ExtTable`) caches its
background colour at component-creation time and does not re-read
`UIManager.getColor("Table.background")` after the LAF is applied. Result:
chrome and menus render dark, but the content area of the download list and
link grabber stays white. This is a JD-side renderer bug and cannot be fixed
from outside JDownloader. A report has been prepared for the JD forum.

## Upgrade

Existing containers: Force Update is enough. `/config` is left untouched
beyond the per-start theme/config re-application.

If the FLATLAF Design-Update or Extensions dialog flashes briefly on first
start after upgrade — that's the agent clicking it for you. Expected behaviour.
